source_text: Εἰ γὰρ σοφία ἀνθρώπου φωτίζει τὸ πρόσωπον, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἀρετὴ γυναικὸς φωτίζει τὴν ὄψιν. Εἰ δὲ μέγαν νομίζεις εἶναι τοῦτον τὸν κόσμον, εἰπέ μοι, τί σοι τὸ ὄφελος ἀπὸ τῶν μαργαριτῶν τούτων ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ γενήσεται; Καὶ τί χρὴ λέγειν τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην, ἐξὸν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν παρόντων ταῦτα ἀποδεῖξαι πάντα; Ὅτε γοῦν οἱ δόξαντες εἰς τὸν βασιλέα ὑβρικέναι, εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον εἵλκοντο καὶ περὶ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἐκινδύνευον, τότε αἱ μητέρες καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τὰ περιδέῤῥαια καὶ τὰ χρυσία καὶ τοὺς μαργαρίτας ἀποθέμεναι καὶ τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα καὶ τὰ ἱμάτια τὰ χρυσᾶ, λιτὴν καὶ εὐτελῆ λαβοῦσαι ἐσθῆτα, καὶ σποδὸν καταπασάμεναι, καὶ πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν τοῦ δικαστηρίου κυλινδούμεναι, οὕτω τοὺς δικάζοντας ἐπέκαμπτον. Εἰ δὲ ἐπὶ τῶν ἐνταῦθα δικαστηρίων τὰ μὲν χρυσία καὶ οἱ μαργαρῖται καὶ ἡ ποικίλη ἐσθὴς ἐπιβουλὴ καὶ προδοσία γένοιτ' ἂν, ἡ δὲ ἐπιείκεια καὶ ἡ πραότης καὶ ἡ τέφρα καὶ τὰ δάκρυα καὶ τὰ εὐτελῆ ἱμάτια μᾶλλον ἐπισπᾶται τὸν δικαστὴν, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐπὶ τῆς ἀδεκάστου ψήφου καὶ φοβερᾶς ἐκείνης γένοιτ' ἂν τοῦτο. Τίνα γὰρ ἕξεις, εἰπέ μοι, λόγον εἰπεῖν, ποίαν ἀπολογίαν, ὅταν ὁ Δεσπότης ἐγκαλῇ σοι περὶ τῶν μαργαριτῶν τούτων, καὶ τοὺς πένητας εἰς μέσον ἀγάγῃ τῷ λιμῷ διαφθαρέντας; Διὰ τοῦτο ὁ Παῦλος ἔλεγε· Μὴ ἐν πλέγμασιν, ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἢ μαργαρίταις, ἢ ἱματισμῷ πολυτελεῖ. Ἐντεῦθεν μὲν γὰρ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ γένοιτ' ἄν· εἰ δὲ καὶ διηνεκῶς αὐτῶν ἀπολαύσαιμεν, ἀλλὰ τῷ θανάτῳ πάντως ἀποστησόμεθα. Ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρετῆς ἀσφάλεια πᾶσα, καὶ μεταβολὴ καὶ μετάπτωσις οὐδεμία, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐνταῦθα ἡμᾶς ἀσφαλεστέρους ποιεῖ, καὶ ἐκεῖ συμμεθίσταται. Βούλει κτήσασθαι μαργαρίτας, καὶ τὸν πλοῦτον τοῦτον μηδέποτε ἀποθέσθαι; περιελομένη τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα εἰς τὰς τοῦ Χριστοῦ χεῖρας ἀπόθου διὰ τῶν πενήτων· ἐκεῖνός σοι φυλάξει τὸν πλοῦτον ἅπαντα, ἐπειδὰν ἀναστήσῃ σου τὸ σῶμα μετὰ πολλῆς τῆς λαμπρότητος· τότε σοι βελτίονα περιθήσει πλοῦτον καὶ κόσμον μείζονα, ὡς ὅ γε παρὼν οὗτος εὐτελὴς καὶ καταγέλαστος. Ἐννόησον οὖν τίσιν ἀρέσκειν βούλει, καὶ διὰ τίνας περίκεισαι τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον, ἵνα ὁ σχοινοστρόφος, καὶ ὁ χαλκοτύπος. καὶ ὁ ἀγοραῖος ἰδόντες θαυμάσωσιν· εἶτα οὐκ αἰσχύνῃ οὐδὲ ἐρυθριᾷς ἐκείνοις ἐπιδεικνυμένη, καὶ οὓς οὐδὲ ἀξίους εἶναι νομίζεις τῆς σῆς προσρήσεως, διὰ τούτους ἅπαντα ποιοῦσα, Πῶς οὖν καταγελάσεις τῆς φαντασίας ταύτης; Ἂν ἀναμνησθῇς τῆς φωνῆς ἐκείνης, ἣν ἀφῆκας μυσταγωγουμένη· Ἀποτάσσομαί σοι, Σατανᾶ, καὶ τῇ πομπῇ σου καὶ τῇ λατρείᾳ σου· ἡ γὰρ περὶ τὸν κόσμον τῶν μαργαριτῶν μανία πομπὴ σατανική ἐστι. Χρυσίον γὰρ ἔλαβες, οὐχ ἵνα τὸ σῶμα καταδήσῃς, ἀλλ' ἵνα τοὺς πένητας λύσῃς καὶ διαθρέψῃς. Λέγε τοίνυν συνεχῶς· Ἀποτάσσομαί σοι, Σατανᾶ· οὐδὲν ταύτης ἀσφαλέστερον τῆς φωνῆς, εἰ διὰ τῶν ἔργων αὐτὴν ἐπιδειξόμεθα. εʹ. Ταύτην καὶ ὑμᾶς τοὺς μυσταγωγεῖσθαι μέλλοντας μαθεῖν ἀξιῶ· αὕτη γὰρ ἡ φωνὴ συνθήκη πρὸς τὸν Δεσπότην ἐστί. Καὶ καθάπερ ἡμεῖς οἰκέτας ἀγοράζοντες, αὐτοὺς τοὺς πωλουμένους πρότερον ἐρωτῶμεν, εἰ βούλονται ἡμῖν δουλεῦσαι, οὕτω καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ποιεῖ· ἐπειδὴ μέλλει σε εἰς δουλείαν λαμβάνειν, πρότερον ἐρωτᾷ, εἰ βούλει τὸν τύραννον ἐκεῖνον ἀφεῖναι τὸν ὠμὸν καὶ ἀπηνῆ, καὶ συνθήκας δέχεται παρὰ σοῦ· οὐ γὰρ κατηναγκασμένη αὐτοῦ ἡ δεσποτεία ἐστί.
thought_title: The renunciation as the weapon against jewelry
orientation: Chrysostom is still addressing the women among the catechumens, arguing that their jewelry is useless and dangerous, and he now turns to the baptismal renunciation of Satan as the remedy.
pass_a_gloss: For if the wisdom of a person makes the face shine, much more does the virtue of a woman make the countenance shine. But if you think this adornment is great, tell me, what benefit will there be to you from these pearls on that day? And why is it necessary to speak of that day, when it is possible to demonstrate all these things also from the present circumstances? When at any rate those who seemed to have insulted the king were being dragged to the law court and were in danger concerning the last things, then the mothers and the wives, having put away the necklaces and the gold ornaments and the pearls and all the adornment and the golden garments, having taken plain and cheap clothing, and having sprinkled themselves with ashes, and rolling before the doors of the law court, in this way they bent the judges. But if in the law courts here the gold ornaments and the pearls and the embroidered clothing would become a plot and a betrayal, but gentleness and meekness and ashes and tears and cheap garments rather draw the judge to oneself, much more would this happen at the incorruptible and fearful verdict. For what word will you have to say, tell me, what defense, when the Master accuses you concerning these pearls, and brings the poor into the midst, destroyed by famine? For this reason Paul was saying: Not in braids, or gold, or pearls, or costly clothing. For from this the plot would arise; but even if we should enjoy them continually, yet by death we shall certainly be separated from them. But from virtue there is all security, and no change and no fall, but it both makes us safer here and departs with us there. Do you wish to acquire pearls, and never to put away this wealth? Having stripped off all the adornment, deposit it into the hands of Christ through the poor; he will guard all the wealth for you, when he raises your body with much splendor; then he will put around you better wealth and greater adornment, since this present one is cheap and ridiculous. Consider therefore whom you wish to please, and for whose sake you wear this adornment around yourself, so that the rope maker and the bronze smith and the market man may see and marvel; then are you not ashamed nor do you blush, displaying yourself to those, and doing everything for the sake of those whom you do not even consider worthy of your address? How then will you laugh at this vanity? If you remember that voice which you uttered when you were being initiated: I renounce you, Satan, and your pageantry and your service; for the madness concerning the adornment of pearls is Satan's pageantry. For you received gold, not in order that you might bind the body, but in order that you might release the poor and nourish them. Say therefore continually: I renounce you, Satan; nothing is safer than this voice, if we display it through deeds. 5. This voice I ask you also who are about to be initiated to learn; for this voice is a covenant with the Master. And just as we, when buying slaves, first ask those who are being sold whether they wish to serve us, so also Christ does; since he is about to take you into slavery, he first asks whether you wish to let go that tyrant, the cruel and harsh one, and he receives covenants from you; for his lordship is not forced.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the devil's display of worldly things; used here for the madness over pearl adornment.
Fixed glossary rendering of the baptismal renunciation formula.
rejected: I turn away from you, Satan

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the agreement made with Christ at baptism.
Glossary gives 'initiation' for μυσταγωγία; the participle here refers to receiving baptismal initiation.
ἀδέκαστος means unbribable, not subject to influence; 'incorruptible' captures the contrast with earthly judges who can be bent.
Rendered as 'gentleness' to match the virtue vocabulary used earlier in the homily for the adornment of the soul.

pass_b_english: For if a man's wisdom makes his face shine, how much more does a woman's virtue make her appearance shine. But if you think this world is something great, tell me: what good will those pearls do you on that day? And why speak of that day, when it is possible to prove all this from the present as well? When those who were thought to have insulted the king were dragged into court and were in danger of losing everything, then their mothers and wives laid aside their necklaces and gold and pearls and all their adornment and their golden garments, took plain and cheap clothing, sprinkled themselves with ashes, and rolled before the doors of the courtroom, and in this way they bent the judges. Now if in the courts here gold and pearls and embroidered clothing would be a plot and a betrayal, while gentleness and meekness and ashes and tears and cheap garments draw the judge to one's side, how much more will this be so at that incorruptible and fearful verdict. For what argument will you have to make, tell me, what defense, when the Master accuses you about these pearls and brings into the midst the poor who were destroyed by famine? This is why Paul said: not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or expensive clothing (1 Timothy 2:9). For from these a plot could arise; and even if we enjoyed them continually, we will certainly be separated from them by death. But from virtue comes all security, and no change or fall; it makes us safer here, and it crosses over with us there. Do you want to acquire pearls, and never to lay aside this wealth? Strip off all your adornment and deposit it into the hands of Christ through the poor. He will guard all your wealth for you, when he raises your body with great splendor; then he will put on you better wealth and greater adornment, since this present one is cheap and ridiculous. Consider, then, whom you want to please, and for whose sake you wear this adornment: so that the rope maker, the bronze smith, and the market man may see you and marvel. And are you not ashamed, do you not blush, displaying yourself for them—doing everything for people you do not even consider worthy of your greeting? How, then, will you laugh at this delusion? If you remember that voice which you uttered when you were being initiated: I renounce you, Satan, and your pageantry and your worship. For the madness over pearl adornment is Satan's pageantry. You received gold not so that you might bind up your body, but so that you might release the poor and feed them. Say, then, continually: I renounce you, Satan. No voice is safer than this, if we demonstrate it through our deeds.

This voice I ask you also to learn, you who are about to be initiated. For this voice is a covenant with the Master. And just as we, when we buy servants, first ask those who are being sold whether they want to serve us, so Christ also does. Since he is about to take you into his service, he first asks whether you want to abandon that cruel and savage tyrant, and he receives a covenant from you. For his lordship is not forced.

problems.quote: But if you think this adornment is something great
problems.source_quote: Εἰ δὲ μέγαν νομίζεις εἶναι τοῦτον τὸν κόσμον
problems.why: κόσμος here means 'the world,' not 'adornment'; contrast is wisdom/virtue vs. world's greatness.
problems.fix: But if you think this world is something great
problems.ruling: κόσμον is 'world,' not 'adornment'; context contrasts wisdom/virtue with world's greatness, not jewelry.

edits.old: But if you think this adornment is something great
edits.new: But if you think this world is something great

fixed: κόσμος here means 'the world,' not 'adornment'; the contrast is between wisdom/virtue and the world's greatness, so the English should read 'this world.'

problems.why: συμμεθίσταται means 'migrates with us' or 'crosses over with us,' not 'departs with us' which suggests leaving.
problems.fix: it crosses over with us there

problems.why: λατρείᾳ means worship/cultic service, not general service; this is Satan's religious worship, not assistance.
problems.ruling: τῇ λατρείᾳ σου in renunciation formula means 'worship,' not generic 'service'; misleads reader.

edits.new: it crosses over with us there

λατρεία means cultic worship, not general service; edited to 'your worship'.

last_rejected.quote: and no change or fall; it makes us safer here, and it crosses over with us there.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐνταῦθα ἡμᾶς ἀσφαλεστέρους ποιεῖ, καὶ ἐκεῖ συμμεθίσταται
last_rejected.why: Source says virtue 'also makes us safer here' (καὶ), but English drops the 'also,' losing the contrast with the preceding security claim.
last_rejected.fix: but it also makes us safer here, and it crosses over with us there.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'it makes us safer here, and it crosses over' naturally implies 'also here' via the paired καί...καί structure; no contrast lost.

last_rejected.why: πλέγμασιν means 'plaitings/braids' but context is jewelry; 'braided hair' conflates with 1 Peter 3:3, not Paul's wording here.
last_rejected.ruling: πλέγμασιν means braids/plaitings; 'braided hair' is standard rendering of Paul's 1 Tim 2:9 citation, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: λατρεία in baptismal renunciation formula means 'service' to Satan, i.e., his cult/worship; but 'worship' alone misses that it's the service of Satan's system.
last_rejected.ruling: λατρεία means worship/service; 'worship' is within normal range for Satan's λατρεία in baptismal renunciation formula.
